draft.title: A significant Islamic practice
card: A religious practice is something believers do that puts their beliefs into action. In Islam, practices are acts of worship, and they also bind believers together as one community, the ummah.

Muslims gather at the mosque at midday on Friday for the congregational prayer, called Jumu'ah. It includes a sermon (khutbah) given by the imam. It expresses belief in one God and brings the local community together.

The hajj is a pilgrimage to Mecca made in the Islamic month of Dhu al-Hijjah. Muslims who are able to afford it and are healthy enough are expected to make it once in their lifetime. Pilgrims from many nations wear simple clothing and perform the same rites, which expresses submission to God and equality before Him.
To explain a practice, link what believers do to what they believe, and then to what it does for the community.
draft.remember: Islamic practices put belief into action and connect Muslims to one another.

a.q: Which statement best explains how Friday prayer expresses Islamic community?
opts: Muslims worship together and hear a sermon as one group
Muslims pray alone so each person can focus on God
Muslims must travel to Mecca to join the prayer
Muslims gather only to elect leaders of the mosque
a.why: Friday prayer is a congregational prayer with a sermon, so believers worship as one group and the local community is strengthened. Praying alone is wrong because the point of Jumu'ah is gathering together at the mosque.
a.clue: Think about what the word congregational means.

b.q: Amira notices that hajj pilgrims from many countries all wear simple clothing and perform the same rites. What belief does this most clearly express?
opts: All believers are equal before God as members of the ummah
Wealthy Muslims hold a higher rank than poorer Muslims
Each nation should follow its own form of worship
Pilgrims must earn forgiveness by completing every rite
b.why: Shared simple clothing and the same rites show that believers stand equal before God and belong to one community, the ummah. Saying that wealthy Muslims hold a higher rank is the opposite of what the shared dress shows.
b.clue: Consider what the matching clothing removes from view.

a.best: Muslims worship together and hear a sermon as one group

b.best: All believers are equal before God as members of the ummah

check.summary: No problems found. The facts about Jumu'ah and the hajj are accurate, both questions have one clearly right answer, and the explanations match the card.
